In [[geometry]], the '''sphenomegacorona''' is a [[Johnson solid]] with 16 equilateral triangles and 2 squares as its faces.

== Properties ==
The sphenomegacorona was named by {{harvtxt|Johnson|1966}} in which he used the prefix ''spheno-'' referring to a wedge-like complex formed by two adjacent ''lunes''&mdash;a [[square]] with [[Equilateral triangle|equilateral triangles]] attached on its opposite sides. The suffix ''-megacorona'' refers to a crownlike complex of 12 triangles, contrasted with the smaller triangular complex that makes the [[sphenocorona]].{{r|johnson}} By joining both complexes, the resulting polyhedron has 16 equilateral triangles and 2 squares, making 18 faces.{{r|berman}} All of its faces are [[regular polygon]]s, categorizing the sphenomegacorona as a [[Johnson solid]]&mdash;a [[Convex set|convex]] polyhedron in which all of the faces are regular polygons&mdash;enumerated as the 88th Johnson solid <math> J_{88} </math>.{{r|francis}} It is an [[elementary polyhedron]], meaning it cannot be separated by a plane into two small regular-faced polyhedra.{{r|cromwell}}

The [[surface area]] of a sphenomegacorona <math> A </math> is the total of polygonal faces' area&mdash;16 equilateral triangles and 2 squares. The [[volume]] of a sphenomegacorona is obtained by finding the root of a polynomial, and its decimal expansion&mdash;denoted as <math> \xi </math>&mdash;is given by {{OEIS link|A334114}}. With edge length <math> a </math>, its surface area and volume can be formulated as:{{r|berman|oeis}}
<math display="block"> \begin{align}
 A &= \left(2+4\sqrt{3}\right)a^2 &\approx 8.928a^2, \\
 V &= \xi a^3 &\approx 1.948a^3.
\end{align}
</math>

== Cartesian coordinates ==
Let <math> k \approx 0.59463 </math> be the smallest positive root of the [[polynomial]]
<math display="block"> \begin{align} & 1680 x^{16}- 4800 x^{15} - 3712 x^{14} + 17216 x^{13} \\ + & 1568 x^{12} - 24576 x^{11} + 2464 x^{10} + 17248 x^9 \\ - & 3384 x^8 - 5584 x^7 + 2000 x^6+ 240 x^5 \\- & 776 x^4+ 304 x^3 + 200 x^2 - 56 x -23 \end{align}</math>
Then, [[Cartesian coordinate system|Cartesian coordinates]] of a sphenomegacorona with edge length 2 are given by the union of the orbits of the points
<math display="block">\begin{align} &\left(0,1,2\sqrt{1-k^2}\right),\,(2k,1,0),\,\left(0,\frac{\sqrt{3-4k^2}}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}+1,\frac{1-2k^2}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}\right), \\
&\left(1,0,-\sqrt{2+4k-4k^2}\right),\,\left(0,\frac{\sqrt{3-4k^2}\left(2k^2-1\right)}{\left(k^2-1\right)\sqrt{1-k^2}}+1,\frac{2k^4-1}{\left(1-k^2\right)^\frac32}\right) \end{align}</math>
under the action of the [[Symmetry group|group]] generated by reflections about the xz-plane and the yz-plane.{{r|timofeenko}}
